subject: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private / VPC requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@finhealth.com>
Cc: Tom Evans <tom.evans@finhealth.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private / VPC requirements

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for taking time today — great to meet you both. Below is a quick recap of what we discussed during the call and proposed next steps so we all have the same priorities. Please flag anything I missed or got wrong.

Summary of pain & goals
- Regulated workloads: FinHealth needs to keep PHI/PII within a customer-managed VPC and meet SOC 2 / HIPAA expectations.
- Data residency: primary production in us-east-1, with controlled replication to us-west-2 for DR.
- Key management: customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) requirement for model input/token encryption and logging.
- Air-gap / on-prem option: some environments will remain air-gapped for particularly sensitive workloads.
- Performance: production latency SLO of ~150ms p95 on short prompts (customer-facing workflows).

Current stack (from the call)
- Frontend & orchestration: FinHealth uses an internal API gateway on AWS (EKS) and currently calls vendor APIs through a private NAT.
- Data storage: encrypted S3 buckets, VPC endpoints, internal ELBs.
- Identity: Okta SSO, SCIM for provisioning.

Success criteria for first phase
- Private deployment (VPC) that keeps all inference traffic within customer-managed subnets and adheres to their egress policies.
- Ability to bring-your-own-KMS keys and rotate them under customer control.
- Auditability: request/response logs (encrypted at rest) and integration with their SIEM.
- Small pilot running 10k monthly requests, demonstrating p95 latency and end-to-end network isolation.

Open items / constraints to validate
1) Network egress: confirm whether outbound internet access is permitted for model updates or if all model artifacts must be pushed via a staging S3 bucket.
2) Air-gapped sites: need a list of candidate sites and whether they accept physical media for model packaging.
3) KMS/HSM: which KMS provider do you want to use (AWS KMS vs vault/HSM)? Any existing HSM inventory?
4) Compliance artifacts: FinHealth requested SOC 2 evidence and architecture diagrams — I attached a checklist and the security prerequisites doc.

Next steps
- I will loop in our solutions lead, Aditya, and our security engineer, Dev, to scope the VPC/network design and the KMS integration.
- FinHealth to confirm the three open items (network egress, list of air-gapped sites, preferred KMS) by EOD Friday (5/15).
- Redwood will follow up with a draft mutual action plan and a quote for a Private deployment + pilot by next week.

Attachments: FinHealth-Security-Reqs.pdf, RWI-private-deploy-checklist.xlsx

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Tel: (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference — Production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments
From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@finhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private / VPC requirements

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and very close. A few clarifications:

- Network egress: for production workloads no outbound internet is allowed. Model updates must be staged into an S3 bucket owned by FinHealth (we can push artifacts there).
- Air-gapped sites: initial pilot will not be air-gapped, but two legacy data centers will be air-gapped and may need physical media for model refreshes in Phase 2. I can send the list tomorrow.
- KMS: we use AWS KMS in our main account for the pilot; long-term we may require external HSM for certain lines of business.

Also adding Tom on the thread for the SIEM/logging questions.

Thanks,
Sara
Director of Platform Security | FinHealth
sara.lewis@finhealth.com

Aditya / Dev — looping you both in per above. Key asks from FinHealth:
- No outbound internet from production inference nodes; model artifacts will be pushed to a customer S3 staging bucket.
- Pilot uses AWS KMS (FinHealth account); long-term HSM possibility.
- Audit logs into their SIEM (we should confirm log format and retention).

Can you two take a quick pass on network and KMS feasibility and call out any blockers? Initial questions from our side:
1) Can our private control plane (for this pilot) be configured to avoid egress while still receiving model updates from a customer-staged S3?
2) For air-gapped sites, what are our options for secure model packaging and offline deployment?
3) Does automated key rotation work with AWS KMS in the customer account, or do we need a hybrid approach?

Aditya — could you propose an initial network diagram and a checklist for the pilot + estimated effort (days) by Monday? Dev — can you outline the KMS/HSM integration options and any security review items we should prepare?

Sara / Tom — we’ll aim to have a technical follow-up call early next week with Aditya and Dev to align on the mechanics. Is Tuesday 5/19 10am ET workable?

Thanks,
Marissa

Quick note on SIEM integration: we use Splunk Cloud; desired fields are request_id, timestamp, model_id, truncated_input_hash, response_status, latency_ms. Retention is 2 years for these logs. We prefer S3 dump + Splunk ingestion via our ingestion pipeline; is that a pattern you support?
